stem: △ABC (blue) was transformed to make △A′B′C′ (red). Is this a rigid transformation?

visual.alt: Triangle ABC and its image A′B′C′

choices.t: No. It is a dilation, so the image is similar but not congruent.
choices.why: Right! Every side doubled, so the size changed but the shape did not.

choices.t: Yes. It is a translation, so the image is congruent.
choices.why: A translation only slides a figure. This image is bigger, so it was not a slide.

choices.t: Yes. The shape stayed the same, so the image is congruent.
choices.why: Same shape is not enough. Congruent figures must also be the same size.

choices.t: No. The shape changed, so the image is not similar.
choices.why: The angles stayed the same and every side doubled, so the shape did not change.

hint: Compare the lengths: is A′B′ the same length as AB?
explain: AB = 3 − 1 = 2 units. A′B′ = 6 − 2 = 4 units. The image is bigger.
Each point was multiplied by 2: A(1, 1) → A′(2, 2). That is a dilation.
A dilation changes size but keeps shape, so it is not rigid. The image is similar, not congruent.

stem: △ABC has A(1, −2), B(5, −2), and C(4, 2). Translate it using the rule (x − 5, y + 3). What are the coordinates of the image?

visual.alt: Triangle ABC with A(1, −2), B(5, −2), C(4, 2)

choices.why: Yes! You moved every point left 5 and up 3.
You moved right 5 and down 3. The rule x − 5 means left 5, and y + 3 means up 3.
You mixed up the numbers. Subtract 5 from x, and add 3 to y.
You subtracted 3 from y. The rule says y + 3, so move up 3.

hint: x − 5 moves each point left 5. What does y + 3 do?
explain: x − 5 means move left 5. y + 3 means move up 3.

stem: △JKL has J(1, 3), K(4, 1), and L(2, −2). Rotate it 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?

visual.alt: Triangle JKL with J(1, 3), K(4, 1), L(2, −2)

choices.why: Correct! The 90° clockwise rule is (x, y) → (y, −x).
You used (x, y) → (−y, x). That is the 90° counterclockwise rule.
You changed both signs without swapping. That is the 180° rule.
You swapped x and y but forgot to change the sign of the new y.

hint: Clockwise means the way clock hands turn. Use the rule (x, y) → (y, −x).
explain: Plot the points: J(1, 3), K(4, 1), L(2, −2).
90° clockwise rule: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap, then change the sign of the new y.

stem: △MNP has M(−4, 4), N(6, 2), and P(2, −6). Dilate it by a scale factor of {{1|2}} with the center at the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?

visual.alt: Triangle MNP with M(−4, 4), N(6, 2), P(2, −6)

choices.why: Yes! You multiplied both coordinates by {{1|2}}.
You multiplied by 2. A scale factor of {{1|2}} means multiply by {{1|2}}, which makes it smaller.
You only changed x. Multiply both x and y by {{1|2}}.
You halved the numbers but dropped the negative signs. Keep each sign.

hint: Multiply each x and each y by {{1|2}}.
explain: Rule: (x, y) → ({{1|2}}x, {{1|2}}y). Multiply both coordinates by {{1|2}}.

stem: △ABC (blue) was dilated about the origin to make △A′B′C′ (red), with A′(3, 1.5), B′(9, 1.5), and C′(3, 6). What is the scale factor, and which check proves it?

visual.alt: Triangle ABC and its larger image A′B′C′

choices.why: Right! Two pairs of sides give the same ratio, 1.5.
You divided original ÷ image. Scale factor is image ÷ original.

choices.t: k = 2, since A′B′ − AB = 6 − 4 = 2
choices.why: You subtracted. A scale factor compares sides by dividing: 6 ÷ 4.

choices.t: k = 6, since side A′B′ is 6 units long
choices.why: 6 is the length of A′B′. Compare it to AB by dividing: 6 ÷ 4.

hint: Find AB and A′B′. Then divide image ÷ original.
explain: Slanted side: BC = 5 and B′C′ = 7.5. {{7.5|5}} = 1.5 ✓
Every pair has the same ratio, so k = 1.5.

stem: △RST maps onto △R′S′T′. Which single transformation does this?

visual.alt: Triangle RST with R(1, 2), S(5, 2), T(5, 4) and image R′(−2, 1), S′(−2, 5), T′(−4, 5)

choices.t: A rotation of 90° counterclockwise about the origin
choices.why: Correct! (x, y) → (−y, x) works for all three points.

choices.t: A rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin
choices.why: Clockwise would send R(1, 2) to (2, −1), below the x-axis. The image went the other way.

choices.t: A reflection across the y-axis
choices.why: A reflection across the y-axis sends R(1, 2) to (−1, 2). R′ is (−2, 1).

choices.t: A rotation of 180° about the origin

hint: Look at R(1, 2) and R′(−2, 1). Did the numbers swap places?
explain: R(1, 2) → R′(−2, 1): the numbers swapped and one sign changed. That means a 90° turn.
The rule (x, y) → (−y, x) is 90° counterclockwise.
So it is a 90° counterclockwise rotation about the origin.

stem: Kayla rotated △ABC 90° clockwise about the origin. She got A′(−5, 2), B′(−1, 4), C′(−3, 1) (red). What was her mistake?

visual.alt: Triangle ABC and Kayla's image

choices.t: She used the counterclockwise rule. Correct: A′(5, −2), B′(1, −4), C′(3, −1)
choices.why: Yes! Kayla used (x, y) → (−y, x). Clockwise is (x, y) → (y, −x).

choices.t: She used the counterclockwise rule. Correct: A′(2, −5), B′(4, −1), C′(1, −3)
choices.why: Right mistake, wrong fix. These points only change the sign of y. That is a reflection across the x-axis.

choices.t: She forgot to swap x and y. Correct: A′(−2, 5), B′(−4, 1), C′(−1, 3)
choices.why: Kayla did swap. These points only change the sign of x, which is a reflection across the y-axis.

choices.t: Her answer is correct. 90° clockwise is (x, y) → (−y, x).
choices.why: (x, y) → (−y, x) is the counterclockwise rule. Her triangle turned the wrong way.

hint: Write the 90° clockwise rule. Does Kayla's A′ match it?
explain: Kayla's A(2, 5) → (−5, 2) fits (x, y) → (−y, x). That is the counterclockwise rule.
90° clockwise is (x, y) → (y, −x).

stem: Rotate △DEF 180° about the origin. Then dilate the result by a scale factor of 2 about the origin. Which rule does both steps at once, and how does the final image compare to △DEF?

visual.alt: Triangle DEF with D(1, 1), E(3, 1), F(1, 4)

choices.t: (x, y) → (−2x, −2y); similar, not congruent
choices.why: Right! Change both signs, multiply by 2, and the size doubles.

choices.t: (x, y) → (−2x, −2y); congruent
choices.why: The rule is right, but the dilation doubles every side. Different size means not congruent.

choices.t: (x, y) → (−x + 2, −y + 2); congruent
choices.why: A dilation multiplies by 2. It does not add 2.

choices.t: (x, y) → (2x, 2y); similar, not congruent
choices.why: You forgot the 180° rotation. It changes the signs of both coordinates.

hint: Do the 180° step on point D first, then the dilation. What happened to D(1, 1)?
explain: Both steps together: (x, y) → (−2x, −2y).
DE = 2 but D″E″ = 4. Same shape, different size → similar, not congruent.

stem: Rectangle WXYZ is dilated by a scale factor of 3 about the origin. Which explanation is correct?

visual.alt: Rectangle WXYZ, 4 units wide and 3 units tall

choices.t: Each side is ×3 and the angles stay 90°, so it is similar. The area goes from 12 to 108, which is 3 × 3 = 9 times as big.
choices.why: Yes! Length and width both grow 3 times, so area grows 3² = 9 times.

choices.t: Each side is ×3 and the angles stay 90°, so it is similar. The area goes from 12 to 36, which is 3 times as big.
choices.why: Area uses two lengths. Each one is ×3, so area is ×9, not ×3.

choices.t: The angles stay 90°, so the new rectangle is congruent. The area goes from 12 to 108, which is 9 times as big.
choices.why: Same angles is not enough. Congruent figures must be the same size, and every side here is 3 times longer.

choices.t: Each side gets 3 units longer (4 → 7 and 3 → 6), so it is similar. The area goes from 12 to 42.
choices.why: A dilation multiplies by 3. It does not add 3.

hint: Find the new length and width first. Then find the new area.
explain: The sides 4 and 3 become 4 × 3 = 12 and 3 × 3 = 9.
Angles stay 90°, and every side is ×3. Same shape, bigger size → similar, not congruent.
Old area: 4 × 3 = 12. New area: 12 × 9 = 108.
{{108|12}} = 9 = 3². Area grows by k² because length and width both get multiplied by k.

stem: △ABC (blue) moved to △A′B′C′ (red). Which transformation is this, and what does it do?

visual.alt: Triangle ABC and its image A′B′C′ on the other side of the y-axis

choices.t: A reflection: it flips the figure across a line.
choices.why: Correct! The image is a mirror image across the y-axis.

choices.t: A translation: it slides the figure without turning it.
choices.why: A slide keeps the figure facing the same way. This image is flipped.

choices.t: A rotation: it turns the figure around a point.
choices.why: A turn would not make a mirror image. Each point here is the same distance from the y-axis on the other side.

choices.t: A dilation: it changes the size of the figure.
choices.why: The image is the same size as the original, so it is not a dilation.

hint: Fold the page along the y-axis. Would the triangles land on each other?
explain: The image is the same size and shape, so it is a rigid transformation.
A(1, 1) → A′(−1, 1) and B(4, 1) → B′(−4, 1). Each point is the same distance from the y-axis, on the other side.
That is a reflection across the y-axis: it flips the figure across a line.

stem: Reflect parallelogram QRST across the x-axis. Which graph shows the image in red?

visual.alt: Parallelogram QRST with Q(−4, 2), R(−1, 2), S(0, 5), T(−3, 5)

choices.why: Yes! Each y changed sign, and each x stayed the same.

t.alt: Image flipped to the right of the y-axis

choices.why: This flips across the y-axis. Across the x-axis, the image goes below it.
This image was slid down, not flipped. A reflection makes a mirror image, so the slant goes the other way.

t.alt: Image turned upside down to the lower right

choices.why: This is a 180° rotation. Both signs changed. Across the x-axis, only y changes sign.

hint: Across the x-axis: (x, y) → (x, −y). Keep x, change the sign of y.
explain: Rule for the x-axis: (x, y) → (x, −y).
The image is a mirror image just below the x-axis.

stem: △GHI is rotated 90° counterclockwise to make △G′H′I′. What are G′H′ and ∠I′?

visual.alt: Triangle GHI with GH = 7 cm, angle G = 62°, angle H = 48°, and its rotated image G′H′I′

choices.t: G′H′ = 7 cm and ∠I′ = 70°
choices.why: Yes! A rotation keeps lengths and angles, and 180° − 62° − 48° = 70°.

choices.t: G′H′ = 7 cm and ∠I′ = 110°
choices.why: 110° is 62° + 48°. Subtract that sum from 180° to find the third angle.

choices.t: G′H′ = 14 cm and ∠I′ = 70°
choices.why: A rotation does not stretch sides. G′H′ = GH = 7 cm. The angle is right: 180° − 62° − 48° = 70°.

choices.t: G′H′ = 7 cm and ∠I′ = 62°
choices.why: ∠I′ matches ∠I, not ∠G. Match the letters: I goes with I′.

hint: A rotation is rigid. What stays the same? Then find ∠I in △GHI.
explain: A rotation is a rigid transformation. It keeps side lengths and angle measures.
So G′H′ = GH = 7 cm.
Angles in a triangle add to 180°: ∠I = 180° − 62° − 48° = 70°.

stem: Are △ABC and △DEF congruent? Which side of △DEF matches BC?

visual.alt: Triangle ABC with A(1, 2), B(5, 2), C(1, 5) and triangle DEF with D(−1, 2), E(−5, 2), F(−1, 5)

choices.t: Yes. A reflection across the y-axis maps A → D, B → E, C → F, so BC matches EF.
choices.why: Correct! A reflection is rigid, and B → E, C → F, so BC ↔ EF.

choices.t: Yes. A reflection across the y-axis maps A → D, B → E, C → F, so BC matches DF.
choices.why: The triangles are congruent, but BC goes with the side whose letters match B and C: E and F.

choices.t: Yes. A translation slides △ABC onto △DEF, so BC matches EF.
choices.why: A slide keeps a figure facing the same way. △DEF is a mirror image, so it was a reflection.

choices.t: No. △DEF faces the other way, so it is not congruent, and no side matches BC.
choices.why: A flip does not change size or shape. Mirror images are still congruent.

hint: Compare B(5, 2) and E(−5, 2). What happened to the x-value?
explain: That is a reflection across the y-axis, a rigid transformation. So △ABC ≅ △DEF.
B → E and C → F, so side BC matches side EF.

stem: Which sequence maps quadrilateral QRST onto Q′R′S′T′?

choices.t: Reflect across the x-axis, then translate by (x − 6, y + 1)
choices.why: Yes! The flip gives Q(1, −1), and the slide moves it to (−5, 0). All four points match.

choices.t: Reflect across the x-axis, then translate by (x − 6, y − 1)
choices.why: After the flip, Q is at (1, −1). To reach (−5, 0) you go up 1, not down 1.

choices.t: Translate by (x − 6, y − 1) only
choices.why: This moves Q and R to the right spots, but S lands at (−2, 2). The image is flipped, so you need a reflection.

choices.t: Rotate 180° about the origin, then translate by (x − 4, y + 1)
choices.why: Q lands on (−5, 0), but R lands on (−8, 0). Check every point, not just one.

hint: The image is upside down. Which step flips it? Then how far does Q need to slide?
explain: Q′R′S′T′ is flipped top-to-bottom, so start with a reflection across the x-axis: (x, y) → (x, −y).
From Q(1, −1) to Q′(−5, 0) is left 6 and up 1: translate by (x − 6, y + 1).

x = 5; perimeter = 33 ft

stem: Which argument correctly proves that △TUV ≅ △KLM (with T → K, U → L, V → M)?

visual.alt: Triangle TUV with T(1, 1), U(3, 1), V(1, 4) and triangle KLM with K(3, −5), L(3, −3), M(6, −5)

choices.t: Reflect across the y-axis, rotate 90° clockwise, then translate (x + 2, y − 6). All three points land on K, L, M, and each step is rigid.
choices.why: Correct! The steps work for every point, and rigid moves keep size and shape.

choices.t: Rotate 90° clockwise, then translate (x + 2, y − 6). Each step is rigid, so the triangles are congruent.
choices.why: Try it: T(1, 1) → (1, −1) → (3, −7). That is not K, so this sequence does not work.

choices.t: Translate (x + 2, y − 6), because T(1, 1) lands on K(3, −5). A translation is rigid.
choices.why: T lands on K, but U lands on (5, −5), not L. You must check every point.

choices.t: TU = KL = 2 and TV = KM = 3. Two pairs of sides match, so the triangles are congruent.
choices.why: Two matching sides are not a proof. You need moves that map the whole triangle onto the other.

hint: Pick a choice and test it on all three points: T, U, and V.
explain: Reflect across the y-axis, (x, y) → (−x, y): T(−1, 1), U(−3, 1), V(−1, 4).
Rotate 90° clockwise, (x, y) → (y, −x): T(1, 1), U(1, 3), V(4, 1).
Translate (x + 2, y − 6): T(3, −5), U(3, −3), V(6, −5). These are K, L, M ✓
Every step is rigid, so the final image is congruent. So △TUV ≅ △KLM.

stem:
Three students want to map △JKL onto △J′K′L′.
• Ana: reflect across the x-axis, then reflect across the y-axis.
• Ben: rotate 180° about the origin.
• Carlos: translate by (x − 4, y − 2).
Which statement is correct?

visual.alt: Triangle JKL with J(2, 1), K(5, 1), L(2, 3) and image J′(−2, −1), K′(−5, −1), L′(−2, −3)

choices.t: Ana's and Ben's both work. Ben's is the most efficient because it uses one step.
choices.why: Yes! Both give the right image, and one step beats two.

choices.t: Ana's and Ben's both work. Ana's is the most efficient because reflections are easier.
choices.why: Ana's does work, but it takes two steps. Ben's single step is more efficient.

choices.t: All three work. Carlos's is the most efficient because it is one simple slide.
choices.why: Carlos only checked J. K(5, 1) moves to (1, −1), not (−5, −1).

choices.t: Only Ana's works, because you need two reflections to reach Quadrant III.
choices.why: Ben's 180° rotation changes both signs too, so it also works.

hint: Test each plan on point K(5, 1). Where should it land?
explain: Carlos: K(5, 1) → (1, −1) ✗, so his plan fails.
Ana's and Ben's both work, but Ben's uses 1 step instead of 2, so it is the most efficient.

stem: Each sequence is applied to a triangle (all moves are about the origin). Which sequence makes an image that is similar but not congruent, and why?

rows: Rotate 90° clockwise, then translate by (x + 1, y + 4)
Reflect across the y-axis, then dilate by {{2|3}}
Reflect across the x-axis, then reflect across the y-axis

choices.t: Sequence 2. The dilation shrinks every side, so the shape stays the same but the size changes.
choices.why: Yes! Similar means same shape, and the dilation by {{2|3}} changes the size.

choices.t: Sequence 3. It uses dilations, and any dilation makes an image that is not congruent.
choices.why: ×2 then ×{{1|2}} is a total scale factor of 1. The size ends up the same, so it is congruent.

choices.t: Sequence 1. The triangle moves to a new place, so it is not the same figure anymore.
choices.why: Moving a figure does not change its size or shape. Rotations and translations make congruent images.

choices.t: Sequence 4. Two flips change the shape of the triangle, so it is only similar.
choices.why: Reflections are rigid. Two reflections still give a congruent image.

hint: Congruent = same shape and same size. Which sequence changes the size in the end?
explain: Congruent figures have the same shape and size. Rigid moves (translate, reflect, rotate) make congruent images.
Similar figures have the same shape, but the size can change. A dilation is needed.
Sequences 1 and 4 use only rigid moves → congruent.
Sequence 3: 2 × {{1|2}} = 1, so the size does not change → congruent.
Sequence 2: the dilation by {{2|3}} shrinks it → similar, not congruent.

stem: Right triangle ABC (blue) is dilated by a scale factor of 1.5 about the origin to make △A′B′C′ (red). AB = 6 and ∠A = 90°. What are A′B′ and ∠A′?

A dilation does not change angles. 90° × 1.5 is not how angles work in a dilation.
You added 1.5 to 6. A dilation multiplies: 6 × 1.5 = 9.
You divided 6 by 1.5. A scale factor greater than 1 makes the figure bigger.

hint: A dilation changes the size. Does it change the angles?
explain: A dilation multiplies every side by the scale factor: A′B′ = 6 × 1.5 = 9.
Check on the graph: A′(−3, 1.5) to B′(6, 1.5) is 6 − (−3) = 9 ✓
A dilation keeps every angle the same, so ∠A′ = ∠A = 90°.
Same angles, sides ×1.5 → same shape, bigger size.

visual.alt: Original triangle with sides 6, 9, 12 cm and copy with sides 4, 6, 8 cm

choices.why: Yes! 4 ÷ 6, 6 ÷ 9, and 8 ÷ 12 all equal {{2|3}}.
You divided original ÷ copy. That is the scale factor from the copy back to the original.
4 is the difference 12 − 8. A scale factor is found by dividing, not subtracting.
Check: 12 × {{1|2}} = 6, but the copy's longest side is 8. Divide 8 ÷ 12.

hint: Scale factor = copy side ÷ matching original side.
explain: Match sides by size: 6 ↔ 4, 9 ↔ 6, 12 ↔ 8.
Every ratio is {{2|3}}, so the scale factor is {{2|3}}. It is less than 1, so the copy is smaller.

stem: Which rectangle is similar to Rectangle 1?

visual.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 440 250"><rect x="50" y="80" width="48" height="120" class="s-blue f-soft" stroke-width="2.2"/><text x="74.0" y="218.0" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700">4 cm</text><text x="44.0" y="145.0" font-size="14" text-anchor="end" font-weight="700">10 cm</text><text x="74.0" y="238.0" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="600" class="t-muted">Rectangle 1</text><rect x="188" y="56" width="72" height="144" class="s-red f-redsoft" stroke-width="2.2"/><text x="224.0" y="218.0" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700">6 cm</text><text x="182.0" y="133.0" font-size="14" text-anchor="end" font-weight="700">12 cm</text><text x="224.0" y="238.0" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="600" class="t-muted">Rectangle 2</text><rect x="350" y="20" width="72" height="180" class="s-gold f-goldsoft" stroke-width="2.2"/><text x="386.0" y="218.0" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700">6 cm</text><text x="344.0" y="115.0" font-size="14" text-anchor="end" font-weight="700">15 cm</text><text x="386.0" y="238.0" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="600" class="t-muted">Rectangle 3</text></svg>
visual.alt: Rectangle 1 is 4 cm by 10 cm, Rectangle 2 is 6 cm by 12 cm, Rectangle 3 is 6 cm by 15 cm

choices.t: Only Rectangle 3, because {{6|4}} = {{15|10}} = 1.5
choices.why: Yes! All angles are 90°, and both side ratios are 1.5.

choices.t: Only Rectangle 2, because each side is 2 cm longer
choices.why: Adding the same amount does not keep the shape. Similar figures multiply by the same number.

choices.t: Both, because all rectangles have four 90° angles
choices.why: Matching angles is not enough. The side ratios must also be equal.

choices.t: Both, because {{6|4}} = 1.5 for each one
choices.why: Check the other pair of sides too. For Rectangle 2, {{12|10}} = 1.2, not 1.5.

hint: Divide the short sides and divide the long sides. Are the two ratios the same?
explain: All three are rectangles, so all angles are 90°. Now check the side ratios.
Rectangle 2: {{6|4}} = 1.5 but {{12|10}} = 1.2. The ratios are different → not similar.
Rectangle 3: {{6|4}} = 1.5 and {{15|10}} = 1.5. The ratios match → similar.
So only Rectangle 3 is similar to Rectangle 1.

stem: △JKL is similar to △RST. Which similarity statement is correct?

visual.alt: Triangle JKL with angle J = 50°, K = 100°, L = 30°, and triangle RST with angle R = 30°, S = 50°, T = 100°

choices.t: △JKL ~ △STR
△JKL ~ △RST
choices.why: The letters must match by equal angles. ∠J = 50° but ∠R = 30°.

choices.t: △JKL ~ △TSR
choices.why: ∠J = 50° goes with ∠S, not ∠T. Match each angle to its equal angle.

choices.t: △JKL ~ △SRT
choices.why: J ↔ S is right, but ∠K = 100° goes with ∠T, not ∠R.

hint: Find the angle in △RST that equals ∠J. Then do the same for ∠K and ∠L.
explain: Match equal angles: ∠J = ∠S = 50°.
Write the letters in the same order: △JKL ~ △STR.
Matching sides follow the order too: JK ↔ ST, KL ↔ TR, JL ↔ SR.

stem: Which sequence maps △PQR onto △XYZ (P → X, Q → Y, R → Z)?

visual.alt: Triangle PQR with P(4, 2), Q(8, 2), R(4, 6) and triangle XYZ with X(−2, −4), Y(−4, −4), Z(−2, −2)

choices.t: Dilate by {{1|2}}, reflect across the y-axis, then translate (x, y − 5)
choices.why: Yes! P → (2, 1) → (−2, 1) → (−2, −4) = X, and Q and R match too.

choices.t: Dilate by {{1|2}}, then translate (x − 6, y − 5)
choices.why: P lands on X, but Q lands on (−2, −4), not Y. Y is to the left of X, so a flip is needed.

choices.t: Dilate by {{1|2}}, reflect across the y-axis, then translate (x, y − 3)
choices.why: After the first two steps, P is at (−2, 1). You need to move down 5 to reach (−2, −4).

choices.t: Dilate by 2, reflect across the y-axis, then translate (x, y − 5)
choices.why: △XYZ is smaller than △PQR. PQ = 4 and XY = 2, so the scale factor is {{1|2}}.

hint: Compare PQ and XY to find the scale factor. Which way does Y sit from X?
explain: PQ = 4 and XY = 2, so the scale factor is {{1|2}}. Dilate: P(2, 1), Q(4, 1), R(2, 3).
Q is to the right of P, but Y is to the left of X. Reflect across the y-axis: P(−2, 1), Q(−4, 1), R(−2, 3).
These are X, Y, and Z ✓

stem: △ABC goes through each sequence. Which choice correctly describes all three final images compared with △ABC?

visual.alt: Triangle ABC with A(1, 1), B(3, 1), C(1, 3), and in red its image after the rule (2x, y), with vertices (2, 1), (6, 1), (2, 3)

rows: Translate by (x + 5, y − 2), then rotate 180° about the origin
Dilate by 4 about the origin, then translate by (x + 1, y − 2)
Apply the rule (x, y) → (2x, y) (shown in red)

choices.t: a) congruent, b) similar, c) neither
choices.why: Yes! a) uses only rigid moves, b) has a dilation, and c) stretches only one direction.

choices.t: a) congruent, b) similar, c) similar
choices.why: In c) only x is doubled. AB doubles from 2 to 4, but AC stays 2, so the shape changes.

choices.t: a) similar, b) congruent, c) neither
choices.why: You switched a) and b). The dilation by 4 is in b), so b) changes size.

choices.t: a) congruent, b) neither, c) similar
choices.why: b) multiplies every side by 4, which keeps the shape. That makes it similar.

hint: Look for a dilation. Then check if c) multiplies every side by the same number.
explain: a) Translation and rotation are both rigid → congruent.
b) Dilate by 4 makes every side ×4, and the translation is rigid → similar, not congruent.
c) (2x, y) gives (2, 1), (6, 1), (2, 3). AB = 2 becomes 4, but AC = 2 stays 2.
The sides are not all multiplied by the same number, so the shape changes → neither.

stem: A small kite frame, △ABC, is similar to a large kite frame, △DEF. Find AC.

visual.svg: <svg viewBox="0 34 440 186"><polygon points="20.0,170.0 112.4,170.0 56.7,127.7" class="s-blue f-soft" stroke-width="2.2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><polygon points="175.0,170.0 406.0,170.0 266.6,64.2" class="s-gold f-goldsoft" stroke-width="2.2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><text x="7.6" y="179.1" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" class="t-blue">A</text><text x="124.9" y="178.6" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" class="t-blue">C</text><text x="53.8" y="120.0" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" class="t-blue">B</text><text x="161.7" y="179.4" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" class="t-gold">D</text><text x="419.5" y="178.8" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" class="t-gold">F</text><text x="263.6" y="55.5" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" class="t-gold">E</text><text x="26.8" y="150.5" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" paint-order="stroke" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="3">8</text><text x="95.9" y="150.1" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" paint-order="stroke" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="3">10</text><text x="69.1" y="187.7" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" class="t-red" paint-order="stroke" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="3">?</text><text x="208.3" y="118.5" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" paint-order="stroke" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="3">20</text><text x="293.6" y="188.7" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" paint-order="stroke" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="3">33</text><text x="220.0" y="212.0" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="600" class="t-muted">△ABC ~ △DEF   (lengths in inches)</text></svg>
visual.alt: Small triangle ABC with AB = 8 in, BC = 10 in, AC unknown; large triangle DEF with DE = 20 in and DF = 33 in

choices.why: Yes! The scale factor is 20 ÷ 8 = 2.5, and 33 ÷ 2.5 = 13.2.
You multiplied 33 by 2.5. △ABC is the small kite, so divide: 33 ÷ 2.5.

choices.t: 21 in
choices.why: You subtracted 20 − 8 = 12, then 33 − 12. Similar figures multiply, they do not add or subtract.

choices.t: 25 in
choices.why: 25 is EF, the side that matches BC. AC matches DF.

hint: Use AB and DE to find the scale factor. Which side of △DEF matches AC?
explain: AB ↔ DE, so the scale factor from small to large is {{20|8}} = 2.5.
AC matches DF = 33 in.
AC = 13.2 in.

stem: Which argument correctly proves that △ABC ~ △DEF?

visual.alt: Triangle ABC with A(1, 1), B(3, 1), C(1, 2) and triangle DEF with D(−3, 3), E(−3, 9), F(−6, 3)

choices.t: Dilate by 3, then rotate 90° counterclockwise. This maps A, B, C onto D, E, F. The dilation keeps angles and multiplies every side by 3, so they are similar.
choices.why: Correct! The steps work, and the reason is right.

choices.t: Dilate by 3, then rotate 90° clockwise. This maps A, B, C onto D, E, F. The dilation keeps angles and multiplies every side by 3, so they are similar.
choices.why: Test it: A → (3, 3) → (3, −3). That is not D(−3, 3). Clockwise turns the wrong way.

choices.t: Dilate by 3, then rotate 90° counterclockwise. This maps A, B, C onto D, E, F. Every step keeps the shape, so the triangles are congruent.
choices.why: The steps work, but the dilation makes every side 3 times longer. Different size means similar, not congruent.

choices.t: Dilate by 3, then rotate 90° counterclockwise. This maps A, B, C onto D, E, F. The dilation multiplies the sides and the angles by 3, so they are similar.
choices.why: A dilation does not change angles. Similar figures have equal matching angles.

hint: Test the steps on point A(1, 1) first. Then read each reason closely.
explain: Rotate 90° counterclockwise, (x, y) → (−y, x): A(−3, 3), B(−3, 9), C(−6, 3) = D, E, F ✓
A dilation keeps every angle and multiplies every side by 3. The rotation changes neither.

stem: At the same time of day, 5-foot-tall Luis casts a 4-foot shadow and a tree casts a 36-foot shadow. How tall is the tree, and why can you use similar triangles?

visual.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 440 200"><line x1="20" y1="170" x2="420" y2="170" class="s-muted" stroke-width="1.5"/><polygon points="60.0,170.0 60.0,17.0 182.4,170.0" class="s-green f-greensoft" stroke-width="2.2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><line x1="60" y1="17.0" x2="182.39999999999998" y2="170" class="s-gold" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><line x1="60" y1="170" x2="60" y2="17.0" class="s-green" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round"/><polyline points="60.0,161.0 69.0,161.0 69.0,170.0" class="s-ink f-none" stroke-width="1.4"/><text x="52.0" y="98.5" font-size="16" text-anchor="end" font-weight="700" class="t-red">h</text><text x="121.2" y="190.0" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700">36 ft</text><text x="60.0" y="9.0" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="600" class="t-green">tree</text><polygon points="320.0,170.0 320.0,153.0 333.6,170.0" class="s-blue f-soft" stroke-width="2.2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><line x1="320" y1="153.0" x2="333.6" y2="170" class="s-gold" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/><line x1="320" y1="170" x2="320" y2="153.0" class="s-blue" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round"/><text x="313.0" y="166.5" font-size="14" text-anchor="end" font-weight="700">5 ft</text><text x="326.8" y="190.0" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700">4 ft</text><text x="326.0" y="143.0" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="600" class="t-blue">Luis</text><text x="300.0" y="60.0" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="600" class="t-muted">sun's rays (dashed) hit</text><text x="300.0" y="78.0" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="600" class="t-muted">both at the same angle</text></svg>
visual.alt: To-scale drawing: a tree of unknown height h with a 36 ft shadow, and Luis, 5 ft tall, with a 4 ft shadow

choices.t: 45 ft. Both make a 90° angle with the ground, and the sun's rays hit at the same angle, so the triangles are similar.
choices.why: Yes! Two pairs of equal angles make the triangles similar, and {{5|4}} = {{h|36}} gives h = 45.

choices.t: 28.8 ft. Both make a 90° angle with the ground, and the sun's rays hit at the same angle, so the triangles are similar.
choices.why: You set up {{5|4}} = {{36|h}}. Put heights on top both times: {{5|4}} = {{h|36}}.

choices.t: 37 ft. Luis is 1 foot taller than his shadow, so the tree is 1 foot taller than its shadow.
choices.why: Similar triangles use multiplying, not adding. The tree's shadow is 9 times as long, so the tree is 9 times as tall.

choices.t: 45 ft. Both triangles have a 36-foot side, so they are similar.
choices.why: The number is right, but the reason is not. Only the tree's triangle has a 36-foot side. The reason is the matching angles.

hint: Write a proportion with height over shadow for Luis and for the tree.
explain: Luis and the tree both stand straight up, so each makes a 90° angle with the ground.
The sun's rays hit both at the same angle at the same time. Two pairs of equal angles → similar triangles.
Height over shadow: {{5|4}} = {{h|36}}.
